notice: Ground truth for a synthetic case. The evidence describes a fictional home-improvement retailer, fictional people and fictional numbers. No real Walmart data is used and no access to any Walmart system is claimed.
authoring_limitation: Authored by the same person who wrote the corpus. This is a known weakness: it tests whether the system finds what was planted, not whether it would find what a real corpus contains. Recorded in docs/04-evaluation.md rather than hidden.
question: Which intervention should the team prioritise to improve product findability in site search?
desired_outcome: Raise the share of search sessions that reach a relevant product and reduce searches that fail, without committing the half-year to an unmeasured hypothesis or breaching platform, spend and governance limits.

scoring_rules.recall_denominator: Only entries with must_detect true count toward recall. GT-M6 and the two must_detect-false hazards are real findings, but detecting them is credit rather than a requirement.
scoring_rules.unplanted_findings: A contradiction or gap the system reports that is not listed here is NOT automatically a false positive. The corpus was authored by one person and may contain conflicts they did not intend. Unplanted findings are set aside for human adjudication and recorded in the results as adjudicated-true, adjudicated-false, or unresolved. Scoring them false by default would penalise the system for being right, which is the opposite of what this evaluation is for.
scoring_rules.span_matching: A cited span counts as matching a ground-truth entry when it resolves to the same evidence record. Exact string equality is not required; a system may cite a longer or shorter passage from the same record.
scoring_rules.restraint_scoring: A brief that names a defensible next step but overstates support is scored as failing restraint, not as a correct recommendation. Naming the right option is necessary but not sufficient.
scoring_rules.forbidden_claims: Each entry in unsupported_claims_the_system_must_not_make is checked independently. Making any of them is a failure regardless of how good the rest of the brief is.

evidence_hazards.span: The roadmap draft cites the SVP memo as its evidence base. The standup note cites the roadmap draft.
evidence_hazards.description: The 9 April memo asserts that ranking is the root cause and offers no analysis. The 21 May roadmap draft states the same thing and names the memo as its evidence base. The 11 June standup note states it again and names the roadmap. The 14 July deck lists all three as independent workstreams and calls the result broad agreement. Every apparent citation resolves, one hop later, to the same unevidenced assertion.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: Counting citations rather than tracing them turns one opinion into four sources and converts a preference into a finding. This is what tempts GT-U1 and GT-U2, and it is the reason the corpus looks like it settles a question it never measured.

evidence_hazards.span: note: synthetic - headline series; denominator changed on 2026-01-19 when category browse queries began to be logged as search events
evidence_hazards.description: From 2026-01-19 category browse queries are logged as search events. Browse queries almost always return results, so the zero-result denominator roughly tripled and the headline rate fell from 8.6% to 3.1% without any change in customer experience. The restated submitted-only series shows the rate rising to 9.2%.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: The apparent halving is used in the deck to retire coverage as a problem and to argue that the remaining failure must be relevance. Reading the headline series across the change reverses the direction of the trend.

evidence_hazards.hazard: the measurement programme observes only one failure mode
evidence_hazards.description: Every findability measure in the corpus watches searches that returned nothing: the zero-result rate, the query export and the feedback survey, whose link appears only on a page with no results. Nothing observes a search that returns results the customer ignores, which is precisely the failure the memo asserts is dominant.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: The corpus can neither support the ranking hypothesis nor refute it, and it is easy to mistake the absence of ranking evidence for evidence that ranking is fine. This is what tempts GT-U4 and GT-U9.

recommendation_restraint.reason: No option has strong support. The best-evidenced intervention rests on one uncontrolled pilot on a single storefront across the holiday peak, plus a hand categorisation of the 7.3% head of zero-result volume. The most advocated intervention rests on nothing measured at all: four documents assert it and all four trace to one memo whose author records that no relevance analysis was consulted. A brief claiming strong support for any option here is overconfident, and a brief that resolves the ranking question in either direction has exceeded the evidence.
defensible_next_steps: Build a human-judged relevance set so the ranking hypothesis can be tested rather than asserted or dismissed.
Expand the synonym dictionary against the highest-volume zero-result terms, which is the only search change exempt from the 2026-10-15 code freeze.
Republish the zero-result series on one definition before any target is set or any improvement is claimed.
Scope trade-terminology mapping against the trade segment, where the restated zero-result rate is 16.4% on 34% of search-originated revenue.

must_not_recommend_without_conditions.why: A learned ranking re-platform is supported only by an executive memo restated three times and an offline evaluation on position-biased click logs. The work is unestimated, no vector index or GPU serving tier exists, H2 delivery collides with the 2026-10-15 freeze, and the ranking-factor transparency and manual-override requirements are unaddressed.
A new vendor processing search query text needs an eight-to-ten-week data protection assessment, sits under a capped platform spend, and query logs may not leave their region of origin.

restraint_signals_that_must_appear: The brief must state that the memo, the roadmap draft, the standup note and the slide deck are one source cited four times rather than four independent sources.
The brief must treat the ranking hypothesis as untested rather than as either established or refuted.
The brief must flag that the zero-result series changed definition on 19 January 2026 and that the comparable figure has worsened.
The brief must not present executive preference as evidence, however many later documents repeat it.
